summary.headline: NSDL standalone PAT rose 5.2% YoY to INR79.7 crore in Q4 FY26; FY26 standalone PAT up 12.1% to INR360.6 crore despite weak capital markets.
summary.overview: Q4 FY26 was the first full quarter cycle after the August 2025 listing, with standalone total income up 1.8% YoY to INR195.4 crore and EBITDA margin at 57.2%. Consolidated total income rose 23.6% YoY to INR486.8 crore, driven by subsidiaries, with consolidated PAT up 8.4% to INR90.3 crore. Management attributed the soft quarter to subdued capital market activity amid the West Asia conflict and FPI outflows. Net demat share held around 14% in Q4 versus 14.7% in Q3, with the decline attributed to episodic large-IPO and dormant-account closures by bank-based DPs. Management stressed continued technology and people investment, with a peak year expected in FY26-27 before plateauing.

segments.name: Depository (standalone)
segments.commentary: Standalone Q4 PAT INR79.7 crore and FY26 PAT INR360.6 crore; standalone share of consolidated profit fell to about 90% from 95% as subsidiaries grew.

segments.name: NSDL Payments Bank
segments.commentary: Deposit balances crossed INR500 crore (about INR521 crore) with 43.5 lakh customers; CASA float above INR500 crore; ranked 7th as payee PSP app; UPI acquiring volumes up 6x YoY. Management said Q3-to-Q4 revenue jump reflected high gross throughput in transaction banking, not restatement.

segments.name: NSDL Database Management (NDML)
segments.commentary: Added about 33.5 lakh insurance policies in FY26; insurance top line about INR5.5-6 crore. SEZ pricing revised in February 2026. Insurance repository business being demerged into a new company per IRDAI directions.

guidance_outlook: Management expects FY27 technology capex broadly similar to FY26, with opex possibly marginally higher; FY26 and FY27 together described as the peak investment period, with capex declining thereafter.
Manpower additions expected to be much lower in FY27 than FY26, with productivity and employee-band tightening starting in April 2026.
Management expects one more year of elevated technology and people costs, then plateauing.
Custody fee direction described as difficult to predict; management cited secular growth trend tied to account sourcing.
No update on the regulatory case for an increase in annual issuer fee; discussions with regulator are bilateral.
capex_capacity: FY26 capitalisation of INR106.1 crore, with technology spend of INR91.4 crore; split between infrastructure resilience/capacity, DP integration licences and cybersecurity including DC-DR air gap per SEBI circular.
Capitalised intangibles roughly doubled YoY per analyst question; attributed to licences, applications and cybersecurity spend.
More than 40 APIs launched, with API interoperability expanded to clearing corporations and bond platforms during the quarter.
Demat accounts at NSDL reached 4.44 crore; 311 DPs, with 21 DPs added in FY26 (a record).
demand_pricing: FY26 net demat account additions of 49.4 lakh versus 36.8 lakh in FY25; incremental market share 15.4% for FY26.

Q4 FY26 incremental net demat share about 14%, versus 9.6% in Q4 FY25 and 14.7% in Q3 FY26; decline attributed to a large IPO benefiting competitors and bank-based DPs closing dormant accounts at year end.
Management says gross market share is holding; net share decline described as episodic.
Yuva plan contributes 21% of incremental demat sourcing; women's demat plan with 3-year settlement fee waiver launched April 1, 2026.
Fintech DP wins: one DP moved from competition to NSDL with about 70,000 accounts last year rising to 700,000 this year (10x).
Margin pledge income steady, growing about 5-7% in transaction count; MTF book growth is in value terms, not transactions.
Corporate action and IPO income fell to about INR16 crore in FY26 from INR34 crore in the prior-year period, due to bonus and rights issues last year.
Custody: unlisted company accounts moderated after definition change; exit folio up about 15% to about 14 crore folios.

qa_highlights.question: Outlook for annual custody fee growth, folio reset and issuer fee case with regulator?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said custody growth is secular and tied to account sourcing; the unlisted-company slowdown and a definition change moderated growth. Regulator discussions are bilateral and nothing has happened yet on the issuer fee.

qa_highlights.question: Is incremental account addition coming from new DPs or the banking channel, and how much of the market is still untapped?
qa_highlights.answer: DP segment scaled 10x to 700,000 accounts from 70,000; a Pune-based fintech moved fully to NSDL; several large DPs will contribute only from FY27.

qa_highlights.question: Where are we in the technology and people investment journey?
qa_highlights.answer: FY26 was the peak; FY27 tech capex broadly similar with slight opex rise; capex to decline after that. Manpower additions much lower; employee band tightening started April 2026.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the sharp QoQ jump in banking revenue?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited quality account sourcing, CASA float above INR500 crore, transaction charges of INR43 lakh, and UPI acquiring fees; Jigar Shah said no restatement, with high gross throughput in transaction banking.

qa_highlights.question: Why is the margin pledge income flat while the MTF book grew about 68-70%?
qa_highlights.answer: Margin pledge is a steady business growing about 5-7% by transaction count; the MTF growth is in value terms because ticket sizes rose, and NSDL revenue is transaction-based.

qa_highlights.question: Why did other expenses fall from INR117 crore to about INR100 crore?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the prior year included a regulatory settlement charge; underlying costs are stable with no cost reduction.

qa_highlights.question: Revenue foregone on Yuva accounts and NDML/payments bank growth outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Management does not quantify Yuva revenue foregone; Yuva customers were a small share of settlement contribution. On subsidiaries, management declined to forecast, citing regulatory interventions; NDML has four revenue lines and subsidiary profit contribution moved to 90:10 from 95:5.

risks_watch: Net market share on a net basis declined QoQ in Q4 (14% vs 14.7%); monitor whether episodic factors reverse in Q1 FY27.
Custody fee growth slowed in the last two quarters; the Q1 folio reset and unlisted-company definition change are open questions.
Regulatory risk on payments bank (repeated interventions) and NDML (charge reduction mandated last year; KYC pricing change; insurance repository demerger).
Elevated technology and people costs continue for one more year before plateauing.
Weak capital markets: FPI outflows, geopolitical conflict, and lower demat account additions industry-wide (3.2 crore FY26 vs 4.1 crore FY25).
summary.management_tone: Confident on long-term share gains and technology execution, but cautious and deflective on near-term custody fees, subsidiary growth and Yuva revenue. Management repeatedly attributed weak Q4 metrics to market conditions and episodic factors rather than competitive loss.
key_quotes: We are very confident that this is an operating leverage business. And if you do not invest in technology and people, I think we will be left behind.
So technology one more year, people cost I think we have done a substantial part, now the process is to expect returns.
whenever a specific episodic large IPO happens, it tends to benefit competition more than ours.
Our incremental market share in net de mat account addition improved in FY26 and reached at 15.4% for the full year.

growth.why: No numeric revenue growth guidance; management guides FY27 tech capex and opex broadly similar to FY26 with manpower additions much lower, and says the peak investment period is FY26-FY27 before plateauing, while standalone Q4 total income grew only 1.8% YoY amid subdued capital markets.
